content:
- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 5–10 days of 30d window).
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and then drop too sharply, suggesting overshoot after spikes.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias — forecasts often revert to historical mean too quickly, missing sustained trends.
- Late-period forecasts (last 10 days) are generally too low, indicating underestimation of downward momentum or delayed correction.
- Model fails to capture sharp downward corrections after high peaks — often underestimates the depth of drops.
- Forecasts show lag in responding to recent price drops — model takes 2–3 days to adjust downward.
- Overconfidence in short-term momentum: forecasts often ignore recent volatility or mean-reversion signals.
- Model tends to overfit recent high prices, leading to inflated forecasts when prices are already trending down.
- Forecasts are overly optimistic in the first 10 days of the 30d window, then become overly pessimistic in the last 10 days.
